title: Kenyan Lamb Curry
community: Especially popular in coastal and Nairobi communities — Indian-Kenyan influence
author: Chef Amina Hassan
desc: Kenyan Lamb Curry — tender bone-in lamb simmered in an aromatic, warmly spiced tomato and onion sauce with curry powder, garam masala, turmeric, and fresh ginger. Richer and more aromatic than beef curry, with a depth that makes it one of the most satisfying curries in the Kenyan repertoire.
longDesc: Lamb curry occupies a special place in Kenyan cuisine — richer than beef, milder than goat, and deeply aromatic when paired with the Kenyan-Indian spice blend. Along the coast and in Nairobi's Indian-Kenyan community, lamb curry is the luxury one-pot meal for special occasions, always served with fragrant rice or freshly made chapati.
ingredients: 1 kg lamb — bone-in shoulder or leg pieces
steps: Brown seasoned lamb in hot oil in batches. Remove and set aside.
Cook onions until deeply golden — 10 minutes.
Add garlic and ginger. Cook 1 minute.
Add tomatoes and tomato paste. Cook for 8—10 minutes until very thick and dark.
Add all spices except garam masala. Stir 1 minute to bloom.
Return lamb. Add stock. Bring to a boil.
Reduce heat to very low. Cover and simmer for 60—70 minutes until the lamb is completely tender.
Stir in garam masala. Taste and adjust seasoning.
chefTips: Allow the tomato-onion base to cook down until very dark and thick — this deep base is the foundation of the curry's flavour.
Bone-in lamb enriches the sauce far more than boneless.
A splash of natural yogurt stirred in at the end creates a creamier, milder version.
commonMistakes: Under-cooking the onion-tomato base — the sauce will taste raw.
Boneless lamb — less flavour and the sauce will be thinner.

faqs.q: Can I add spinach or potatoes?
faqs.a: Yes — both work beautifully. Add potatoes 25 minutes before the end; add spinach in the last 5 minutes.

cookingScience: Lamb fat contains short-chain fatty acids that are highly aromatic when heated. The longer the lamb cooks in the spiced sauce, the more these flavour compounds integrate into the curry, creating a more unified, complex flavour profile.
sustainabilityTips: Use shoulder pieces — a less popular cut that benefits from slow cooking and supports whole-animal butchery.
storage: Refrigerate for up to 4 days. Freeze for up to 3 months.
reheating: Reheat gently on stovetop with a splash of water.
healthBenefits: Rich in complete protein — 36g per serving.
Good source of iron and B12.
culturalNote: Lamb curry reflects Kenya's long history of Indian-Kenyan cultural exchange, particularly in coastal cities and Nairobi. It is a celebration dish — served at family gatherings, Eid feasts, and restaurant occasions where something special is called for.
regionalVariations: Coastal coconut lamb curry — with coconut milk.
Dry lamb curry — sauce reduced to a coating.
Yogurt lamb curry — with natural yogurt for creaminess.
Spicy lamb curry — with extra chilli.
